answer: Random Harbored Seed Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function derives a seed no one can predict before it is published, then deterministically maps that seed to admission slots on a fixed reef of shards. An identity must land its slot on its assigned shard; mismatches are rejected. Because the mapping shifts every epoch, attackers cannot precompute which shards to flood, so each fake identity needs separately provisioned credentials and presence across an unpredictable karst of shard assignments.
